initial_posts.content: DBS CEO Piyush Gupta's pay rose to S$15.4 million in 2022, a 13% increase as the bank hits record S$8.19 billion profit. Read more on Mothership.

Proud to announce that DBS has achieved a record net profit of S$8.19 billion. This success is a testament to our team's resilience in a challenging year and our commitment to being the World's Best Bank.
I just wrote about the breakdown of Piyush Gupta's S$15.38M package. While the bank's performance is stellar, the timing with current inflation rates is definitely going to spark a conversation.
Record profits for the bank, but my savings interest can't even keep up with GST hikes. S$15 million for one man while the rest of us struggle with inflation is a bit much, isn't it?
Our 2022 performance reflects our ability to navigate high inflation and bearish markets. We remain focused on our sustainability goals and digital transformation across Asia.
DBS continues to set the benchmark for banking excellence globally, maintaining its position as the World's Best Bank through innovation and strong leadership.

event_config.narrative_direction: The discourse will likely begin with objective reporting of the record profits and the CEO's pay rise, but will rapidly shift toward a polarized debate. Retail customers and low-income workers will express frustration over the widening wealth gap during a period of high inflation, while financial analysts and institutionalists will defend the compensation as a fair reflection of market-leading performance. The narrative will likely peak around the 'reputational risk' of a 13.3% pay hike (reaching a risk score of 7/10) as the public fixates on the disparity between corporate success and individual financial struggle.
